explanation: I searched every Mathlib file that mentions IsValuativeTopology: Topology/Algebra/ValuativeRel/ValuativeTopology.lean, Topology/Algebra/Valued/ValuativeRel.lean, WithVal.lean, Padics/ValuativeRel.lean, Padics/HeightOneSpectrum.lean, LocalField/Basic.lean and RamificationInertia/Valuation.lean. Mathlib only declares IsValuativeTopology instances for particular settings: the topology defined from a valuative relation (ValuativeRel.isValuativeTopology), WithVal v and ℚ_[p]. It also has a low-priority instance going the other way, from IsValuativeTopology back to Valued. There is no lemma saying that an arbitrary `Valued R Γ₀`, with the relation ValuativeRel.ofValuation hv.v, gives a valuative topology. The library's proof builds this from the constructor IsValuativeTopology.of_mem_nhds_zero_iff_vle, together with Valuation.Compatible.ofValuation and Valued.mem_nhds_zero. That combination is the library's own contribution, and the constructor alone does not carry the result.
